summary: Pro-Router is a serving-layer cascade for multimodal LLMs. A prompt pre-scorer sends easy requests to a small edge model (Qwen2.5-VL-7B, LLaVA-OneVision-7B or Pixtral-12B). A CPU-side two-layer transformer then reads the small model's per-token sampling distributions to decide whether its answer ships or escalates to a cloud Qwen2.5-VL-72B. A Ray/vLLM scheduler sizes dispatches to each device's measured service rate. Evaluated on 15 VQA/text QA benchmarks against RouteLLM, FrugalGPT, P(True) and AutoMix.

claims.claim: The token-aware verifier has the highest routing accuracy of all baselines on every small model.
claims.evidence: Figure 4 shows mean AUROC, macro PGR, AUARC and AUACC averaged over 15 benchmarks, as bar summaries without CIs. Table 2 gives full AUROC of 0.805 / 0.753 / 0.685 for Qwen / LLaVA-OV / Pixtral. Correctness labels come from an LLM judge whose validity is not reported.

claims.claim: The routing signal is more than 10× faster than prior methods.
claims.evidence: Figure 5: 2–3 ms vs 47–119 ms for the scorer baselines (19–28×), and seconds to minutes for P(True)/AutoMix.

claims.claim: The pipeline gives more than 75% higher end-to-end throughput than the existing routing pipeline.
claims.evidence: Figure 6b: 1.77–1.79× vs a Ray Serve deployment graph that sends every request to the small model first. That baseline is the authors' own expression of the policy, not a tuned production system.

claims.claim: Throughput is robust to network latency and scales linearly with devices.
claims.evidence: Figure 7: 90–96% of un-delayed throughput at 200–1000 ms injected delay. Linear scaling up to M=3, N=4 (5.8–6.9× a single cloud device). Single runs, no variance.

patterns.note: Small→large model cascade with confidence-based escalation from per-token logits. This requires self-hosted models with logit access and applies to multimodal QA, not coding agents.
Optimizes throughput and serving cost, but reports no dollar or token budgets.

methodology.sample: 15 benchmarks with roughly 106–682 test items each (Table 1).
methodology.baselines: RouteLLM, FrugalGPT, P(True), AutoMix, 'reproduced faithfully' with verbatim templates. Plus a Ray Serve pipeline for throughput.
methodology.models: Small: Qwen2.5-VL-7B, LLaVA-OneVision-7B, Pixtral-12B. Large: Qwen2.5-VL-72B.
methodology.variance: None reported. No seeds, CIs or repeated runs.
methodology.ablations: Verifier input features, verifier depth/architecture, and pipeline optimizations (batched dispatch, KV-cache gate), all in Table 2.
methodology.languages: n/a. Multimodal and text QA, no code.

biases.detail: Correctness labels for routing accuracy come from an LLM judge with no reported agreement with humans.
All figures are single-run point estimates.
The throughput baseline is a naive small-first Ray Serve graph built by the authors.
Multimodal VQA serving infrastructure, not software engineering or coding agents.

coi.affiliations: Anyscale; Mississippi State University; Institute of Computing Technology, CAS; Institute of AI for Industries, CAS. Per-author mapping is lost in the text extraction.
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Built on Ray (Anyscale's open-source framework) and compared favorably against a Ray Serve pipeline. No Anyscale commercial product is promoted.
coi.detail: Vendor affiliation (Anyscale) on a Ray-based system. The comparison is against the vendor's own open framework, so there is no self-promotion of a product.

verdict_reason: Off-topic: serving-layer routing for multimodal VQA with logit access to self-hosted models. It does not address coding agents or SE harnesses. Results also lack variance and rely on an unvalidated LLM judge.
applicability: Does not transfer. The team consumes hosted frontier models through mixed agent hosts, and the repo invariants leave cheap-vs-expensive model choice to the host or an opt-in gateway, so a per-token-logit verifier inside a vLLM serving stack is not something the harness can or should own. The only generic lesson is that confidence-gated escalation from a cheap model to an expensive one can recover most quality at lower cost, which a gateway the host points at might use. Nothing here bears on Java, multi-repo work or spec-driven development.
